Some friends have asked, why can't we feel the vibrancy of the economy when the stock market is rising?

Many people believe that the higher the stock market rises, the better the economy is, but this is an extremely misguided view. As the stock market rises, institutional risks become more exposed, and the underlying debts and leverage also expand. A rising market implies higher asset pricing, greater financing needs, and larger credit expansion. When the stock market rises to a certain extent, there will also be a decline in expected returns on assets, and asset prices will naturally diverge from the credit system, leading to the formation of a boundary between bull and bear markets.

A frenzied rise in the stock market forces the entire financial system to expand in sync, which means banks must provide more funding exposure, the credit system is forced to expand, and the debt exposure grows larger. Because all large institutions operate under the same consensus, liabilities do not decrease while assets expand.

Therefore, using the stock market to measure economic vibrancy is a flawed standard. The role that cryptocurrencies currently play, especially Bitcoin, is the 'risk premium' of traditional financial markets. Over the past two years, it has been repeatedly emphasized that Bitcoin's asset attribute has become 'a safe-haven asset, not a risky asset,' but almost no one believes it, as most people cannot understand that in traditional financial markets, the higher the asset prices rise, the higher the risk premium.

I believe that in the coming time, you will gradually understand this theory. With the continuous increase of risk exposure in the traditional market, the crypto market will soon enter a phase of takeoff. At that time, you will feel that some large institutions and Fortune 500 companies are rushing in to maintain the vitality of their assets.

The seven giants of the U.S. stock market will gradually enter the market.

有小伙伴问，股市上涨为何感受不到经济的活跃度？

在许多人认知里股市涨幅越高经济越好，但这是一个极其错误的观点。股市越涨，机构的风险暴露越大，背后的债务与杠杠也会随之膨胀，一个上涨的市场意味着更高的资产定价，更高的融资需求以及更大的信用扩张，当股市上涨到一定程度同时也会出现资产预期回报的下降，资产价格自然会脱离信用体系，从而导致牛熊分界线形成。

股市疯狂上涨，会强迫整个金融系统同步的扩张，也就意味着银行必须提供更多资金敞口，信贷系统被迫扩容，债权敞口越来越大。因为所有的大型机构，都在同一共识下运行，负债不降，资产膨胀。

所以用股市衡量经济活跃度，是一个错误的标准，而加密货币目前承担的角色，尤其比特币是传统金融市场的“风险溢价”，过去两年反复强调比特币的资产属性已经成为“避险资产，而非风险资产”，但几乎没人相信，在于大多数人理解不了传统金融市场资产越涨风险溢价越高。

我相信在接下来时间里，你会逐渐理解这套理论，以目前传统市场的风险敞口不断加码、加密市场接下来会进入起飞状态，到时候你会感受到一些大型机构和世界500强公司疯狂入场以保持自己资产的活力。

title: 两大央行背道而驰，加密货币市场迎来“流动性风暴”！
subTitle:
当美联储与日本央行同时转动政策方向盘，却指向相反方向时，全球资本的洪流正被搅得天翻地覆。
作为一名长期跟踪全球流动性与加密货币关联的分析师，我清晰地感受到2025年12月将成为决定市场方向的关键月份。美联储与日本央行即将上演的“政策错位”，正在引发一场全球资本流动的风暴。
市场预期美联储12月降息25个基点的概率已升至84.9%，而日本央行加息的概率也攀升至80%以上
。这种罕见的政策分化，将重新定义未来半年加密货币市场的运行逻辑。

 两大央行的政策错位：当美联储与日本央行背道而驰
当前全球货币政策正呈现罕见的分化态势，两大主要央行走向截然相反的方向。
美联储的“鹰派降息”困境。市场普遍预期美联储将在12月9-10日的会议上降息25个基点
。但这很可能是一次充满矛盾的“鹰派降息”——一方面降低利率，另一方面却释放对未来降息步伐的谨慎态度。

美联储主席鲍威尔面临的核心困境在于如何平衡“通胀顽固”与“增长承压”的矛盾
。尽管降息概率高企，但美联储不会轻易放弃遏制通胀的承诺，这意味着任何宽松都将是有节制的、试探性的。

日本央行的历史性转向。相比之下，日本央行正准备进行17年来的首次加息
。日本央行已于3月结束负利率政策，将基准利率从-0.1%~0上调至0~0.1%。而市场现在预期，日本央行在12月18-19日的会议上可能进一步加息。

日本央行这一决策基于国内工资明显增长（2024财年日本大型公司同意将工资提高5.28%，为1991年以来最大涨幅）以及通胀率连续超过2%的目标
。这意味着全球最后一个维持超低利率的主要经济体正在“改弦更张”。

三条核心传导路径：流动性如何影响加密货币市场
这两大央行的政策转变将通过三条路径直接影响加密货币市场。
廉价日元退场，套息交易平仓。过去十年，全球金融市场的一大“隐形福利”是日元的零成本资金。一旦日本央行加息，意味着全球最主要的融资货币成本将系统性抬升
。

大量借入日元、投资美元资产（包括美债、美股、加密货币）的“套息交易”将被迫平仓。这种平仓可能导致资金从风险市场流出，回流日本，直接抽离全球美元流动性。历史数据显示，日元升值往往引发套利交易平仓，进而冲击高风险资产
。

加密货币市场首当其冲。作为高波动性资产的代表，加密货币对此类全球流动性收紧极为敏感
。例如，2025年8月，当市场对美联储降息预期减弱时，比特币曾一度跌破115，000美元，导致超过13万人爆仓。

回顾2025年11月，比特币价格一度跌破90，000美元，为4月以来首次，自10月初创下的126，250美元历史高点回撤近30%
。这表明在流动性收紧环境下，加密货币的脆弱性暴露无遗。

美债吸引力下降，全球利率“地板”抬高。日本央行加息将收窄美日利差。对于持有超万亿美元美国国债的日本投资者而言，在对冲汇率风险后，美国国债的相对吸引力正在下降
。

这可能引发资金从美国国债市场撤出，推高被视为“全球资产定价之锚”的美国国债收益率。而美债收益率的上升将提高全球资产的贴现率，压制包括加密货币在内的风险资产估值。
市场影响：高波动时代与去杠杆风险
这场流动性风暴对市场的影响将是深远且复杂的。
短期影响：高波动和“踩踏式”去杠杆。美元流动性在美日政策错配下可能进一步趋紧，市场可能出现“避险”与“缺钱”共存的局面。过去24小时内，加密货币市场爆仓总金额达3.01亿美元，超过10万人被爆仓的情况可能重演
。

对加密货币市场的冲击。虽然美联储降息从长期看是流动性利好，但这一利好可能被日本加息引发的全球杠杆平仓潮所对冲。加密市场的脆弱性使其在混乱中极易出现放大式的下跌。
诺贝尔经济学奖得主保罗·克鲁格曼对比特币的批评值得思考，他认为“比特币未能找到实际用途，其表现得更像一只波动性更高的科技股”
。在这种市场环境下，任何反弹都可能因流动性不足而缺乏持续性。

长期影响：旧时代的落幕。从更宏观的视角看，这场风暴标志着一个依赖“廉价日元”的全球流动性旧时代正在落幕。所有高风险资产，包括加密货币，都必须在一个资金成本更高、波动更剧烈的“新常态”中重新寻找定价逻辑。
 我的应对策略：如何在风暴中生存与获利
面对即将到来的市场风暴，我分享个人的应对策略。
仓位管理是生存之本。在市场高波动期，我将严格执行“总仓位不超过本金50%”的纪律，确保有足够现金应对极端行情。历史教训表明，在市场剧烈波动中，超过11万人曾在24小时内爆仓，严格的仓位管理是避免成为其中一员的關鍵
。

关注关键位置与市场情绪。比特币90，000美元是关键心理关口
。若能守住这一防线，市场有望企稳；若失守，下一个支撑位可能在4月份接近74，000美元的低点。

利用波动而非被波动利用。在市场恐慌抛售时，我会有选择地分批建仓优质资产。正如一位分析师所指出的，现货ETF的资金流动数据表明，市场下跌更多是资本轮动所致，而非投资者信心崩溃
。

保持政策敏感性。我会密切关注12月两大央行的实际政策决定与后续表述，尤其是美联储主席鲍威尔和日本央行行长植田和男的讲话。央行行长的措辞变化往往比政策本身更能预示未来方向。
当美联储与日本央行在12月各自做出政策决定后，全球流动性格局将迎来重塑。对于敏锐的交易者而言，波动不是风险，而是机会。
“在这个市场里，活得久比赚得快更重要。”作为一名穿越多次牛熊周期的分析师，我认为未来几周的关键不是预测单一政策，而是管理好自身风险敞口，警惕由政策错配引发的连锁流动性风险。#BTC #ETH 如果你正陷入套单迷茫丶不知道怎么操作，关注我，用实战经验帮你避坑指路，稳稳守住本金，慢慢赚收益！

title: Fusaka Upgrade: Experts Defend the Odd-Looking Gas Cap, Calling It the Key to Parallelization
subTitle:
Ethereum’s Fusaka upgrade has officially gone live, sending ETH to $3,222 and marking a significant leap forward for the network’s scalability roadmap. The update raises the block gas limit to 60 million and introduces a per-transaction gas ceiling of 16.78 million — a configuration that has stirred debate among developers but is widely praised for enabling parallel execution and preventing resource overload.

A Technical Breakthrough for Scaling and Lower Fees
The Ethereum blockchain has rolled out the Fusaka upgrade, and early reactions call it a major success in advancing the network’s long-term roadmap. The market responded almost instantly. Ether surged to $3,222 shortly after the upgrade, its highest level since November 17. The move was striking given that ETH had traded near $2,800 just a day earlier on December 2, underscoring strong market conviction in the protocol’s latest transformations.
Arriving roughly seven months after the transformative Pectra upgrade, Fusaka is being celebrated for delivering deep technical improvements that reshape Ethereum’s capacity. These enhancements move the network closer to its longstanding promises of dramatically lower and more predictable Layer-2 (L2) fees, along with a major expansion in throughput.
The core mechanism driving this shift is the combination of lifting the block gas limit to 60 million and introducing the Transaction Gas Limit Cap (TGLC) at precisely 16.78 million gas. The specific value raised eyebrows across the developer community. Some critics argued the number appeared arbitrary, chosen without the public modeling and technical justification expected for a parameter that influences worst-case block processing time.
Still, engineers and protocol researchers have pushed back on that criticism. The per-transaction ceiling, they argue, is exactly what the network needs to prevent a single transaction from monopolizing node resources.
Mo Dong, Brevis CEO and co-founder, highlighted the technical precision of the choice. He explained that the 16.78 million threshold works well because “a power-of-two–like structure simplifies implementation across multiple codebases.” More importantly, he said, “this limit enables parallelization,” allowing nodes to process transactions more efficiently by distributing work.
Charles d’Haussy, CEO of the dYdX Foundation, echoed this view. He noted that the cap preserves the ability to execute large transactions without risking delays or opening the door to denial-of-service vectors. In his assessment, developers selected this number because it is “large enough not to disturb typical activity, but small enough to preserve predictable execution times and safeguard the network.”
L2 Scaling, Security, and the PeerDAS Debate
The Fusaka upgrade also introduces Peer Data Availability Sampling (PeerDAS) and expands potential blob capacity by as much as eightfold. This has triggered intense debate about how much L2 fees will fall and which rollup architectures stand to benefit most.
Experts interviewed widely agree that PeerDAS will deliver meaningful reductions in L2 costs, but not at a perfectly linear ratio to capacity increases. Ivo Georgiev, CEO and founder of Ambire Wallet, estimates that the maximum reduction probably tops out around 80%. “It’s not as simple as expecting fees to fall 8x,” he said. “But given the added overhead of today’s rollup transactions, a 30–40% reduction is almost guaranteed.”
PeerDAS fundamentally changes how Ethereum processes blob data. Instead of requiring every node to fully replicate all data, the network distributes data availability proofs across participants. This architectural shift addresses Ethereum’s long-standing scalability bottleneck but also invites scrutiny over latency and data security.
Dong described the design as a calculated technical tradeoff that unlocks massive scalability while preserving Ethereum’s underlying integrity. The main security advantage, he said, is its resilience against data-withholding attacks.
“In hostile scenarios where a block producer withholds data, the sampling mechanism provides cryptographic assurances that missing data will be detected with overwhelming probability. Analyses show the likelihood of a successful attack dropping to effectively zero — around one in 10²⁰ — as network size increases,” Dong noted.
Georgiev added that in practical terms, PeerDAS introduces “almost no tangible downside — it’s virtually a pure win.”
Critics, however, warn that PeerDAS could introduce systemic risks tied to block validity and temporary data unavailability, issues developers must proactively assess. Even so, d’Haussy expressed confidence that these concerns will not translate into fundamental new threat vectors.
“Sampling actually makes it harder to finalize a block that contains missing data, because validators only vote once they confirm availability. The primary risk window is short-term — a temporary network delay that could cause missed attestations,” he explained.
Despite the ongoing technical debates, both supporters and skeptics agree on one point: Fusaka strengthens Ethereum’s position as the secure, decentralized settlement layer for a multi-chain ecosystem. By unlocking new levels of throughput and cost efficiency, it accelerates L2 economics and prepares the network for its next wave of innovation — scaling up without compromising the foundational principles that made Ethereum dominant in the first place.

subTitle:
以太坊的价值演进已从“世界计算机”迈向“全球结算层”，其投资逻辑核心在于生态扩张、价值锚定、货币属性、全栈金融、开放生态和长期前景六大维度。

一、平台化扩张：从L2扩展到生态闭环​

以太坊通过Rollup等L2方案降低交易成本、提升吞吐量，吸引DeFi、NFT等应用积累用户基数，形成“用户增长→生态繁荣→结算需求上升”的正循环。随着主网TPS提升及Danksharding等技术落地，其逐步承载支付、资产交易等大额结算，类似互联网“先聚流量后变现”的逻辑。

二、价值锚定：TVL驱动估值体系​

ETH的估值下限与生态总锁仓量（TVL）高度关联。应用繁荣推高手续费收入，而RWA（现实世界资产代币化）等趋势持续抬升TVL。若稳定币规模达3万亿美元、RWA达20万亿美元，ETH市值有望对应突破3万亿美元。

三、货币属性：从支付工具到结算底层​

ETH已超越支付工具范畴，成为全球货币体系的“结算层”。其支撑稳定币发行、跨链清算及复杂金融逻辑，在AI时代的小额高频结算（如算力交易）中扮演关键角色。

四、全栈金融：覆盖资产发行到商业自动化​

以太坊支撑美股代币化、RWA等资产发行，并通过DeFi协议提供存款、借贷等银行服务。同时赋能供应链金融、去中心化市场等商业场景，实现“发行-交易-结算”全链路自动化。

五、开放生态：开发者友好与场景无界​

以太坊的护城河在于其开放性：支持多语言开发，拥抱AI、RWA等新场景，并通过智能合约实现金融逻辑可编程化，打破传统金融的地域和中介限制。

六、长期前景：从金融OS到全球结算底层​

短期通过L2扩容聚集生态，中期推动RWA落地扩大TVL，长期目标成为AI时代覆盖支付、资产、金融的全域结算底层，价值空间随生态扩张持续打开。

以太坊的终极愿景是成为“金融的Windows”，通过开放性生态重塑全球金融基础设施。

The value evolution of Ethereum has progressed from 'world computer' to 'global settlement layer,' with the core investment logic focusing on six dimensions: ecological expansion, value anchoring, monetary attributes, full-stack finance, open ecology, and long-term prospects.

1. Platform expansion: from L2 to ecological closed loop​

Ethereum reduces transaction costs and increases throughput through L2 solutions like Rollup, attracting applications such as DeFi and NFTs to accumulate a user base, forming a positive cycle of 'user growth → ecological prosperity → increased settlement demand.' As the mainnet TPS improves and technologies like Danksharding are implemented, it gradually supports large settlements for payments and asset transactions, similar to the internet's logic of 'first gathering traffic and then monetizing.'

Today this DOGE is behaving too strangely. Clearly, the ETF application news is coming one after another, and there's a lot of activity on the chain, so why is the price dropping instead, even breaking key levels? On the news front, big players like Grayscale are lining up to apply for ETFs, which is clearly a long-term positive; the number of active addresses on the chain has also surged to over 70,000, indicating that the number of users hasn't decreased. With market sentiment in "Extreme Fear" and $BTC seeing outflows, all eyes are on Ethereum and the recent Fusaka upgrade. Experts are pointing to a major shift: The new protocol could trigger a supply crunch that hasn't been seen in years!
What do you need to know?
A "Rollup-First" Ethereum: Instead of processing everything on Layer 1 (L1), Ethereum is now a settlement layer, relying on Layer 2 (L2) rollups like Arbitrum, Optimism, and Base for the bulk of transactions.
The Problem: Until now, L2s have benefited from L1 security without contributing much to the ETH burn, leading to net inflation.
Fusaka's Solution: The latest upgrade introduces EIP-7918, which mandates that Layer 2 transactions contribute to the ETH burn. Projections suggest this could burn an additional 200,000–400,000 ETH per year, potentially making ETH net deflationary again.
How does it work? The PeerDAS system makes rollup data cheaper and more plentiful by sampling it, rather than requiring full downloads. This increased efficiency allows L2s to thrive, but it also increases the total $ETH  burn as more L2 activity is generated.
For the average user, what does this mean?
Lower L2 Fees: You'll likely see lower transaction costs on your favorite rollups, making everyday DeFi and NFT activities cheaper.
Long-Term Bullish Pressure: If the burn rate accelerates as projected, the resulting supply scarcity could add upward pressure to the price of $ETH  over the long run, even in a cautious market.
The Big Question:
With the Fusaka upgrade now live, will institutional adoption follow and accelerate ETH's deflationary path, or will the broader market downturn limit its impact?

subTitle:
比特幣的功能主要是「轉帳」，但區塊鏈能做的遠不只如此！
這就要提到「智能合約 (Smart Contract)」。簡單來說，它是一段寫在區塊鏈上的程式碼，只要滿足條件，就會自動執行。就像一台自動販賣機：你投錢（滿足條件），它掉出飲料（執行結果），完全不需要店員操作。
這讓區塊鏈可以拿來做金融借貸 (DeFi)、發行 NFT、甚至遊戲。
以太坊 (ETH) 以太坊是智能合約的始祖與龍頭。在這個生態系上的每一次操作，都需要支付 ETH 作為燃料費 (Gas)。這意味著，只要區塊鏈應用越繁榮，對 ETH 的需求就越大。這也是為什麼 ETH 被視為最具實用價值的加密貨幣。

translatedData.title: 【Technical Applications】If Bitcoin is digital gold, then Ethereum is the 'World Computer'
translatedData.subTitle:
The main function of Bitcoin is 'transfer', but blockchain can do much more than that!
This brings us to 'Smart Contracts'. In simple terms, it is a piece of code written on the blockchain that automatically executes when conditions are met. It's like a vending machine: you put in money (meet the conditions), and it dispenses a drink (execution result), without any need for a clerk to operate.
This allows blockchain to be used for financial lending (DeFi), issuing NFTs, and even gaming.
Ethereum (ETH) is the pioneer and leader of smart contracts. Every operation in this ecosystem requires paying ETH as a gas fee. This means that as blockchain applications become more prosperous, the demand for ETH increases. This is why ETH is considered the most practical cryptocurrency.

LINK Vs ETH

Part 1

Ethereum (ETH) is a foundational blockchain platform for building decentralized applications (dApps) and executing smart contracts.
Chainlink (LINK) is a decentralized oracle network that connects smart contracts on blockchains, including Ethereum, with real-world data and off-chain systems.
ETH is the native cryptocurrency of the Ethereum network, used to pay for transaction fees (gas) and as a store of value.
LINK is the native token of the Chainlink network, used to incentivize node operators for providing accurate and tamper-proof off-chain data to smart contracts.
Chainlink enhances Ethereum's utility by allowing its smart contracts to interact with external data, which they cannot do natively.

Ethereum (ETH) and Chainlink (LINK) serve distinct but complementary roles within the blockchain ecosystem. Ethereum is a robust, general-purpose blockchain platform that enables developers to create and deploy smart contracts and decentralized applications. Its native cryptocurrency, Ether (ETH), functions as the "fuel" for the network, covering transaction fees (known as gas) and serving as a store of value.

In contrast, Chainlink is a decentralized oracle network built to address a critical limitation of blockchains: their inability to directly access real-world data. Chainlink acts as a "bridge" between on-chain smart contracts and off-chain data sources, events, and traditional systems. The LINK token is integral to the Chainlink network, used to compensate node operators who retrieve and deliver this external data to smart contracts, ensuring its accuracy and reliability.

content:
Blockchain Security

Part 1

Blockchain networks safeguard transaction data primarily through cryptography, decentralization, and consensus mechanisms.
Cryptographic hash functions create unique digital fingerprints for each block, linking them securely and making any tampering immediately detectable.
Public-key cryptography uses private keys to digitally sign transactions, authenticating the sender and ensuring non-repudiation.
Decentralization distributes the ledger across numerous nodes, eliminating single points of failure and preventing unauthorized changes by any one entity.
Consensus mechanisms require network participants to agree on transaction validity, ensuring data integrity and preventing fraudulent entries.

A blockchain network employs several robust mechanisms to safeguard and authenticate transaction data, making it highly secure and resistant to tampering. At its core, cryptography plays a fundamental role. Cryptographic hash functions generate a unique "digital fingerprint" for each block of transactions. Each new block includes the hash of the previous block, creating an unbreakable chain. If any data within a block is altered, its hash changes, breaking the chain and making the tampering evident across the network.

Furthermore, public-key cryptography is crucial for authentication. Users possess a pair of keys: a public key that can be shared and a private key that must be kept secret. When a transaction is initiated, it is digitally signed with the sender's private key. Other network participants can then use the sender's public key to verify this signature, confirming the transaction's authenticity and ensuring that it originated from the rightful owner (non-repudiation).

Decentralization is another key security feature. Instead of relying on a central authority, a blockchain operates on a distributed network of computers (nodes). Each node typically holds a copy of the entire blockchain.

title: ETH Gains Momentum vs BTC Post-Fusaka$3,200 Breakout Setup Activates
subTitle:
Ethereum is trading over $3,100 on Friday. Bulls want to break through a resistance trendline that has been in place for two months.

After the Fusaka update, demand for Ethereum grows, making it stronger versus Bitcoin.

Data from the blockchain suggests that big wallet investors are more interested, but the derivatives and ETF markets are still divided.

Ethereum (ETH) is up more than 1% at the time of writing on Friday. It is still having trouble around the point where the local resistance trendline and an above supply zone meet. After the Fusaka update on Wednesday, demand for the main cryptocurrency has grown among significant wallet investors. This makes it stronger versus Bitcoin (BTC) in the near run. 

The markets for derivatives and ETH-focused Exchange Traded Funds (ETFs) are still mixed, nevertheless. 

Fusaka update makes Ethereum stronger than Bitcoin
On Wednesday, Ethereum released its Fusaka update, which raised the gas cap so that more transactions could fit in each block and perhaps lowered gas prices. The update also adds minimal blob costs to stop gas fees from going to zero during quiet times, and PeerDAS, which makes nodes use less storage and bandwidth while increasing blob capacity by eight times. 

Ethereum rose about 4% versus Bitcoin on Wednesday after new infrastructure was released. It closed above the resistance trendline that connects the highs of August 24 and October 27 on the daily logarithmic chart. 

At the time of writing, the ETH/BTC pair is up 1% on Friday and is trying to close above a range of prices that have been stable since November 10, when it hit a high of 0.03442 BTC, and November 24, when it hit a low of 0.03209 BTC. If the price closes above this level, it might confirm the bullish breakout of the range and make the main cryptocurrency even stronger versus Bitcoin. It's interesting to note that the altcoin season generally corresponds with a jump in ETH/BTC. This might mean that the market as a whole is willing to take on more risk.

On the other hand, the Fusaka upgrade hasn't changed the fact that validator entrance and exit rates and queue times are still going down. This shows that staking momentum is steadily decreasing.

Derivatives data and ETF flows show that Ethereum doesn't have long-term interest from consumers and institutional investors. The CoinGlass data reveals that ETH futures Open Interest (OI) was $37.61 billion on Friday, which is around the same as it was in early November. This suggests that investors are less interested.

The long/short ratio chart, on the other hand, reveals that bearish positioning building has gone down in the previous 24 hours, from 54.22% on Thursday to 50.75% on Friday. 

On Thursday, US spot ETH ETFs saw a net outflow of $41.57 million, after a positive inflow of $140.16 million the day before when the Fusaka update was released. The absence of clear information on institutional backing following the upgrading sends mixed messages to institutional investors. 

On-chain holders, on the other hand, are still optimistic. The total amount of ETH held by big wallet investors with 1 million to 100 million ETH rose from 75.86 million ETH on October 1 to 80.28 million ETH on Friday. 

In general, on-chain holders' confidence stays the same, but retail and institutional support changes a lot with the overall market circumstances.

Will Ethereum go beyond $3,200 in the near future?

Ethereum is having trouble getting over the $3,200 mark because of an overhead resistance trendline that connects the daily highs from October 7 and 27. This trendline is the last piece of a bigger falling wedge formation, which usually leads to an upward breakout. 

Ethereum has to stay above the support-turned-resistance zone between $3,225 and $3,287 at the end of each day to prove the breakthrough. If ETH breaks out, it might go up to the next resistance zone, which is between $3,643 and $3,682. 

The daily chart's momentum indicators offer a signal that is neutral to optimistic. The Relative Strength Index (RSI) is at 51, which is close to the midway line. At the same time, the Moving Average Convergence Divergence (MACD) shows that the market is still bullish, as the average lines move higher and become closer to the zero line. 

But if Ethereum can't stay above $3,000, it might go down to Monday's low of $2,716.

content:
NEAR Vs ETH

Consensus & Scalability: Both NEAR and Ethereum use a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism. However, they approach scalability differently. NEAR was built with a native sharding technology called Nightshade, which processes transactions in parallel across multiple shards to increase throughput. Ethereum is scaling through Layer-2 solutions like rollups.
Performance: NEAR generally offers faster transaction speeds and lower fees compared to Ethereum. NEAR's architecture allows for a theoretical throughput of up to 100,000 transactions per second (TPS), with transaction finality in 1-2 seconds. Ethereum's throughput is lower, and while Layer-2s improve this, they can introduce complexities like delayed finality.
Architecture: NEAR shards both state and processing, meaning validators only need to handle transactions for their specific shard, which lowers hardware requirements. Ethereum's sharding roadmap has evolved, with the core chain now focusing on security for Layer-2s rather than native execution sharding.
Developer Experience: NEAR aims for a more web-developer-friendly experience, using languages like Rust and AssemblyScript and offering features like human-readable account names. Ethereum's ecosystem is more mature and larger, but can be more complex, primarily using the Solidity language.
Ecosystem & Interoperability: Ethereum has a significantly larger and more established ecosystem of dApps, developers, and users. NEAR's ecosystem is growing but is smaller. NEAR facilitates interoperability with Ethereum through tools like the Rainbow Bridge, allowing asset transfers between the two chains.

title: Bitcoin Holds Near $92K as Solana, XRP, ETH Extend Losses; Market Awaits Direction Amid Macro Uncert
subTitle:
Bitcoin hovered around $92,000 on Friday, extending a multi-week stretch of choppy and directionless trading, with major altcoins sliding deeper into the red. The market tone remains cautious, shaped by thin liquidity, macroeconomic uncertainty, and clear signs of capital rotation inside crypto.
Bitcoin Still Trapped in a Descending Structure
The one-month chart continues to show BTC locked inside a descending formation from early November’s highs. The latest rebound once again produced a lower high, peaking near $93,500 before rolling over — keeping the broader corrective trend firmly intact.
BTC remains capped below $93,000, a zone that is well defended by sellers. Meanwhile, dips toward $91,000 have repeatedly attracted buyers; the market thus remains stuck in a tightening range without a decisive breakout.
Momentum indicators remain soft, with intraday recovery attempts quickly fading — a sign that liquidity above spot levels remains thin. A clean breakdown below $91,000 would set sights on the $90,000–$90,500 support pocket, while a firm close above $93,200 is what bulls need to invalidate the short-term downtrend.
Pressure on Altcoins
Large-cap performance was mixed heading into the weekend:
Solana was down 4% and trading at $34.71.
XRP is down almost 5%
Cardano (ADA) shed 2%
Ether (ETH) traded around $3,150 after modest overnight losses.
Market-wide capitalization gained about 1% in the last 24 hours, up to around $3.2 trillion as the slow recovery from the seven-week downturn continues.
ETH notably led major assets over the past week, up more than 5%, while Zcash (ZEC) was up in an outsized rally earlier in the session.
ETF Flows Reveal Clear Capital Rotation
ETF data showed quite a divergence:
Spot Bitcoin ETFs saw $14.9M in net outflows.
Spot Ether ETFs saw a huge inflow of $140.2M
The flows suggest fresh institutional capital is rotating from BTC into the Ethereum ecosystem, likely driven by narratives around ETH's improving fundamentals, upcoming upgrades, and growing use in on-chain finance.
Liquidation data further underscores the divergence.
BTC witnessed $45M in long and $50.7M in short liquidations.
ETH witnessed $103M in short liquidations, indicating that traders were aggressively positioned against ether - and very caught off guard.
Macro Risks Return as U.S. Labor Data Misses
U.S. ADP payrolls dropped 32,000 in November, well below expectations. Wage growth cooled while futures markets now price in a 90% probability of a rate cut in December.
The dollar index was on a sharp swing as traders reset their expectations of rates, while risk markets, including crypto, experienced an uptick in volatility.
Analysts: BTC Faces the Real Test at $98K–$100K
FxPro senior analyst Alex Kuptsikevich also pointed out that Bitcoin’s brief movement to $94,000 faced “not yet too aggressive” resistance. He has reiterated that more vigorous pushback is likely in the $98,000–$100,000 area, which for now remains the key zone to watch for any attempt at a sustained recovery.
Whether the recent rebounds of BTC mark the start of a broader trend shift, or simply corrective bounces, depends on how price action reacts at higher levels.
Market in a 'Composite Phase'
Analysts at Bitunix called the prevailing market setting a "composite phase" dominated by expectations of macroeconomic turning-points and continued internal capital rotation within crypto.
They expect further volatile, range-bound trading until BTC decisively holds above $93,000 or breaks below $90,500.
Institutional Tailwinds Provide Support
Despite the uncertainty, some institutional developments have helped to bolster sentiment:
Vanguard opened crypto ETF trading access to clients
Bank of America told institutional customers they may allocate 1%–4% of portfolios to digital assets.
CME launched a bitcoin implied volatility index, with ETH, SOL, and XRP versions on the way These moves underpin the rapid institutionalization of the crypto market, even as the short-term price action remains range-bound and reactive to macro signals.#BTC #sol #ETH $BTC

content:
SUI Vs ETH

Part 1 

Sui is a modular, object-oriented Layer-1 blockchain designed for high throughput and low latency, while Ethereum is a monolithic, account-based Layer-1 network.
Sui utilizes the Move programming language, which is designed for security and parallel execution, whereas Ethereum primarily uses Solidity.
Sui achieves higher transaction speeds (TPS) and lower finality times through parallel transaction execution, contrasting with Ethereum's sequential processing and lower TPS.
Ethereum has a significantly larger and more mature ecosystem, market capitalization, and broader adoption, especially in DeFi, compared to Sui, which is a newer, rapidly growing network.
Sui aims for lower and more predictable transaction fees, with some dApps even covering gas fees for users, while Ethereum's gas fees can be higher and more variable.

Sui and Ethereum are both Layer-1 blockchain networks, but they differ significantly in their architecture, performance, and ecosystem maturity. Ethereum, launched in 2015, is a well-established, monolithic blockchain that operates on a Proof-of-Stake (PoS) consensus mechanism. It is known for pioneering smart contracts and decentralized applications (dApps), forming the backbone of much of the decentralized finance (DeFi) and NFT space. Ethereum's architecture is account-based and processes transactions sequentially, which can lead to lower transaction throughput (TPS) and higher, less predictable gas fees, especially during periods of high network congestion.

title: Ethereum shows early signs of a rebound as big buyers return
subTitle:
Ethereum has had a rough few months. It is the second biggest crypto by value yet it stayed under three thousand two hundred for more than twenty days. Many traders were scared and sold at lower prices which kept the mood weak. But the latest signs now show that this down move may be close to ending.

For the last three days the market has wiped out many short positions. This means traders who were betting on lower prices got liquidated as the price moved against them. When this kind of sweep happens for several days it often marks a top or a bottom because it clears out big pools of liquidity. In this case it is the shorts that got hit which means the pressure from sellers has become lighter. This gives bulls a better chance to take back control.

After this cleanup the whales are coming back. These are the wallets that hold large amounts and often move the market. One whale moved ten million worth of stablecoins and bought Ethereum again after sitting out for a long time. This shows fresh trust in the asset. Another whale known for large moves also took a long position worth about twenty nine million in Ethereum and is already sitting on profit. This trader usually adds more when the trend goes in their favor so this move tells us they see strength building in the market.

The spot market has also started to warm up. Traders here buy the real asset instead of using leverage. After many days of selling the spot flow has flipped and buyers have spent about forty seven million to load up on Ethereum. The rise in volume also shows interest coming back. When spot buyers return it often means they see a clear reason to enter again.

Data also shows that the earlier hype and overheated trading has cooled down. When this happens the market often finds a better place to bounce. It makes the next move more stable because there is less fear of a sharp drop from high leverage or wild activity.

Ethereum still sits below key levels but the recent events tell a simple story. Bears are losing strength. Whales are buying. Spot traders are back. Liquidity has shifted in favor of the bulls. If this pattern continues Ethereum may have already set its bottom for now.

Nothing here is a promise of fast gains but the changing signs point to a better outlook. As long as buyers keep stepping in and big wallets stay active the price has room to climb from this zone.

Some friends have asked, why can't we feel the vibrancy of the economy when the stock market is rising?

Many people believe that the higher the stock market rises, the better the economy is, but this is an extremely misguided view. As the stock market rises, institutional risks become more exposed, and the underlying debts and leverage also expand. A rising market implies higher asset pricing, greater financing needs, and larger credit expansion. When the stock market rises to a certain extent, there will also be a decline in expected returns on assets, and asset prices will naturally diverge from the credit system, leading to the formation of a boundary between bull and bear markets.

A frenzied rise in the stock market forces the entire financial system to expand in sync, which means banks must provide more funding exposure, the credit system is forced to expand, and the debt exposure grows larger. Because all large institutions operate under the same consensus, liabilities do not decrease while assets expand.

Therefore, using the stock market to measure economic vibrancy is a flawed standard. The role that cryptocurrencies currently play, especially Bitcoin, is the 'risk premium' of traditional financial markets. Over the past two years, it has been repeatedly emphasized that Bitcoin's asset attribute has become 'a safe-haven asset, not a risky asset,' but almost no one believes it, as most people cannot understand that in traditional financial markets, the higher the asset prices rise, the higher the risk premium.

I believe that in the coming time, you will gradually understand this theory. With the continuous increase of risk exposure in the traditional market, the crypto market will soon enter a phase of takeoff. At that time, you will feel that some large institutions and Fortune 500 companies are rushing in to maintain the vitality of their assets.

The seven giants of the U.S. stock market will gradually enter the market.

title: Can Solana pass Ethereum in 2026
subTitle:
This year has opened the door for real use in crypto. Big firms and payment apps are now testing and using chains for daily work. This is very different from the early days when crypto was only about trading. Now chains must show real use and steady speed. Developers are also more active with thousands of full time builders working on major chains.

Ethereum is still the main chain with the biggest group of full time builders. Solana is in second place but it is moving fast. Both chains want to scale and reach bigger markets. This is why every upgrade and every partnership matters now.

The payments world has become the main focus this year. Many firms want faster and cheaper payments. One of the main names here is Revolut. It is a large digital bank in Europe with many users who already hold and move crypto. Revolut has now started to use Solana for cheaper and faster activity on chain. This gives Solana a strong real use example because people can now move funds on Solana rails in daily life.

This move also came soon after a major Ethereum upgrade called Fusaka. Both chains are trying to show that they are ready for big use. Solana has strong points like fast blocks low fees and very high transactions per second. This is why it fits well with the payments market. Revolut using Solana shows that big firms trust its speed.

On the other side Ethereum upgrades have made it stronger too. After earlier upgrades Ethereum saw more use and better speed. The same trend is starting to show after Fusaka. In the last week of November Ethereum saw a rise in activity as users prepared for the change. Solana still keeps a huge lead in daily use because it handles millions of non vote transactions every day. This shows that Solana is already working at a very large scale.

Even with this strong activity Solana has not seen the same price rise as Ethereum. The SOL to ETH ratio has been weak this year. It is down almost twenty percent. This shows that the market values Ethereum more even though Solana is showing faster growth on chain. This gap is now a major topic because many people think Solana is underpriced based on its use.

Next year this gap might start to close. Solana has a big upgrade planned for early 2026 called Alpenglow. This upgrade can push Solana to a new level in speed and scale. If that happens the market may start to value Solana closer to how much it is used in the real world.

Solana has strong on chain numbers and rising trust from firms like Revolut. Ethereum is still ahead right now but Solana is moving up with real speed. The coming year will show how both chains grow and how much Solana can close the gap in use and value.

Ethereum ($ETH ): A Simple, Clear Overview

Ethereum is one of the world’s most influential blockchain platforms. Unlike Bitcoin—which mainly works as digital money—Ethereum acts as a powerful programmable network. Developers can build decentralized applications (dApps), smart contracts, NFTs, DeFi systems, and many other blockchain-based tools on top of it.

Why Ethereum Matters

Smart Contracts: Self-executing digital agreements without intermediaries.

DeFi Ecosystem: Thousands of financial apps run on ETH, enabling lending, trading, and staking without banks.

Strong Developer Community: Ethereum has the largest group of blockchain developers.

ETH as Gas: Every action on the network requires ETH, giving it practical demand.

Proof-of-Stake (PoS): Since “The Merge,” ETH uses far less energy and allows staking rewards.

Strengths of ETH

Large adoption and network effect

Constant upgrades improving speed, fees, and scalability

Institutional interest and real-world use cases growing

Risks to Consider

Competition from faster blockchains

Regulatory uncertainty

Market volatility

High network fees during peak times

So… Buy or Sell? (In Short)

I cannot give personal financial advice — but here’s a neutral, rational guideline:

Buy ETH if you believe in long-term blockchain adoption, Ethereum’s upgrades, and its dominant role in DeFi and smart contracts.

Sell ETH if you expect short-term volatility, need liquidity, or think competing blockchains will overtake Ethereum.

In short:
👉 #ETH ETH is generally considered a strong long-term project, but short-term price movements can be unpredictable.

- Nếu báo cáo PCE thấp hơn dự báo (dưới 2.9% YoY), thị trường sẽ hiểu đây là tín hiệu rõ ràng cho lãi suất giảm sớm, kéo theo:
  - Giảm áp lực lên đồng USD và lợi suất trái phiếu kho bạc 10 năm → tăng dòng vốn vào tài sản rủi ro như #BTC , #ETH .  
  - #XRP  và #SOL  — vốn nhạy cảm với thanh khoản và tâm lý đầu cơ — có thể bật tăng mạnh hơn so với #BTC  nếu có đòn bẩy từ tin tức tích cực.  
- Ngược lại, nếu PCE cao hơn kỳ vọng, thị trường có thể phản ứng bằng đợt điều chỉnh nhanh, đặc biệt với các altcoin như #SOL  và #XRP  — vốn đang trong xu hướng giảm nhẹ và thiếu điểm tựa kỹ thuật mạnh.
Kết luận:
-》Báo cáo lạm phát thứ Sáu không phải là “tin tốt hay xấu”, mà là bộ lọc lựa chọn: nó sẽ làm rõ liệu thị trường có đủ điều kiện để bước vào giai đoạn tăng giá bền vững hay chỉ tiếp tục đi ngang trong trạng thái chờ đợi. Với dữ liệu hiện tại, #BTC  và #ETH  đang ở vị trí phòng thủ tốt; #XRP  và #SOL  cần tin tích cực để thoát khỏi áp lực bán gần đây.
Các thông tin chỉ mang tính tham khảo, không phải lời khuyên đầu tư.
